rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.dragao.e1: Attack: with the king castled, the pawns in front guard the squares around it. A pawn that advances stops guarding the squares it left behind, and they can become weak squares.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.dragao.e2: This is the Dragon Variation of the Sicilian Defence. Black advanced the g-pawn and put the bishop on g7, in fianchetto. With no pawn on g7, the bishop is what guards f6 and h6.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.dragao.l1: The bishop goes to h6, the square the g-pawn stopped guarding, and offers to trade the g7 bishop.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.dragao.l2: Black accepts the trade and captures the bishop.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.dragao.l3: The queen recaptures and arrives next to the king. Without the bishop, h6 has become a weak square: no black pawn reaches it, and f6 has lost a defender.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.dragao.l4: In positions like this, the attacker trades off the defender of the weak squares. Before applying the idea, check how many defenders are still left near the king.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.err.g5h7.1: With this move, Black has a resource: the f6 knight captures your d5 knight.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.err.g5h7.2: Back to the position: the f6 knight defends h7. Look for a move that removes it.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.err.h6h7.1: With this move, Black has a resource: the f6 knight captures the queen on h7.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.err.h6h7.2: Back to the position: the f6 knight defends h7. Look for a move that removes it.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.err.h5g6.1: With this move, Black has a resource: the h1 queen comes down the h-file and captures your queen.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.err.h5g6.2: Back to the position: the f6 knight defends h7. Look for a move that removes it.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.e1: Attack: this position comes from a Caro-Kann played on Lichess. The white queen sits on h6, the weak square the g-pawn left when it advanced.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.e2: The queen and the g5 knight attack the h7 pawn. The king and the f6 knight defend it.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.p: Find the move that exploits the weakness on h7.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.certo: The d5 knight captures the f6 knight with check. It is the removal of the defender: without the f6 knight, the h7 pawn is defended only by the king.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.revela: The d5 knight captures the f6 knight with check and removes the defender of h7.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.fora: That move does not touch the defenders of h7. Look for a move that removes one of them.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.volta: Try again: look at who defends h7.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.l0: The queen and the g5 knight still aim at h7, and the black king is in check.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.l1: The e7 pawn recaptures the knight. Had the king gone to h8, the mate on h7 would be the same.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.l2: The queen captures the h7 pawn with mate, defended by the g5 knight.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.l3: The queen reached h6 through the weak square. With the f6 knight traded off, h7 ran out of defenders. When a pawn closes the king's file, the attacking piece can also give itself up to open it.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.regra.1: Attacking demonstration: a game from Lichess. The white f6 pawn has entered the weak square Black's pawns left behind and guards g7. The queen on h6 and the g3 rook aim at the king.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.regra.2: The queen captures the h7 pawn with check and gives itself up, to open the h-file.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.regra.3: The king has to capture the queen: it is the only move.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.regra.4: The rook goes to h3 with mate: the f6 pawn guards g7, and Black's own g8 rook takes the king's last square.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.regra.5: With no black pawn able to reach f6, the white pawn took over the squares around the king, and the h-file decided.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.regra2.1: Attacking demonstration: again a game from Lichess. The h6 bishop and the f6 knight occupy weak squares around the black king, but the bishop shuts the h-file for your rook.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.regra2.2: The bishop captures the g7 knight with check and opens the h-file for the rook.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.regra2.3: The king has to recapture: it is the only move.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.regra2.4: The rook captures the h7 pawn with mate, defended by the f6 knight.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.regra2.5: The weak squares on h6 and f6 brought White's pieces close to the king. With the h-file open, the rook gave mate.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.excecao.1: Defensive demonstration: now let us think from Black's side. Back to the Dragon: the white bishop went to h6 to trade your g7 bishop. Look at the b3 bishop, which aims at f7 and your king.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.excecao.2: The knight goes to c4 and attacks the queen on d2.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.excecao.3: The b3 bishop captures the knight. This way Black trades off one of the pieces that were attacking the king.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.excecao.5: The h6 bishop trades off the g7 bishop.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.excecao.6: The king recaptures and now guards f6 and h6 from close by.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.excecao.7: With the b3 bishop traded and the king and knight close by, the weak squares matter less. Before attacking a weakness, count the defenders.
The queen captures on h7 with check, but the f7 rook recaptures. The f8 knight still defended the square: remove it first.
The knight captures on h7, but the black queen checks on a1, and mate comes on your back rank. Look for a forcing move.
The queen captures on g6 with check, but the h7 pawn recaptures, and Black is a queen up. Look at the defender of h7.
rot.kingWeaknesses.pratica.valeAqui.enun: Your h6 queen and g5 knight attack h7, but the f8 knight and the f7 rook defend it. Is it worth capturing on h7 straight away here, or must you prepare? Play as White and find the best move.
rot.kingWeaknesses.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The rook captured the f8 knight with check, and the black rook, forced to recapture, left the seventh rank. With both defenders gone, the queen mated on h7, defended by the g5 knight.
rot.kingWeaknesses.pratica.casaF6.err.d5: The knight checks on e7, but the king goes to g7, and the attack stops. Look for a weak square closer to the king.
rot.kingWeaknesses.pratica.casaF6.err.d6: The rook trades rooks on d8, and the game is level. Look for a weak square for the knight, near the king.
rot.kingWeaknesses.pratica.casaF6.enunci: Black's e- and g-pawns have advanced. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.kingWeaknesses.pratica.casaF6.fim: The knight entered f6 with check: the e-pawn has already passed that square, and the g-pawn advanced. The king went to g7, and the rook mated on h7, defended by the knight. Had the king gone to h8, the mate would be the same.
rot.kingWeaknesses.pratica.pretas.err.f5: The rook goes to h5, but the d7 pawn captures your c8 rook and promotes with mate. Look for a move with check.
The rook captures the knight, but the d7 pawn captures your c8 rook and promotes with mate. Look for a move with check.
rot.kingWeaknesses.pratica.pretas.err.h3: The queen checks on g2, but the g1 rook captures it. Look for the square where giving up the queen opens the h-file.
rot.kingWeaknesses.pratica.pretas.enunci: Now let us think from Black's side. White's g3 pawn has advanced, and your f3 pawn guards g2. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.kingWeaknesses.pratica.pretas.fim: The queen gave itself up on h2, the king captured it, and the rook mated on h5: the f3 pawn guards g2, and White's own g1 rook takes the king's other square.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.err.d5e7.1: With this move, Black has a resource: the king goes to h8, and the f6 knight still defends h7.
rot.kingWeaknesses.ideia.caro.err.d5e7.2: Back to the position: the f6 knight defends h7. Look for a move that removes it.
The knight captures on f7, but the black queen checks on a1, and mate comes on your back rank. Look for a forcing move.
The rook drops back to e1, and Black gains time to defend the king: the attack loses its force. Look for a move with check.
rot.kingWeaknesses.pratica.pretas.err.c8: The rook goes to g8, but the b3 queen captures it with check, and mate follows. Look for a move with check.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.cravado.1: Attacking demonstration: another game from Lichess. Black's f6 and g6 pawns have advanced, and the white queen has entered h6. The h7 pawn defends g6, but it is pinned: if it moves, the queen gives check down the h-file.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.cravado.2: The knight captures the g6 pawn with mate. The h7 pawn cannot recapture, and g7 is guarded by the queen and the e6 knight.
rot.kingWeaknesses.demos.cravado.3: In positions like this, check whether the defender can really leave its square: a pinned pawn does not defend.
The pawn goes to h4, but it is slow: the c2 pawn promotes with check, and mate comes first on your back rank. Look for a move with check.
rot.kingWeaknesses.pratica.casaF6.err.d6: The rook leaves d6, and the d5 knight is left undefended: the black rook captures it. Use the knight now, with check.
rot.kingWeaknesses.pratica.casaF6.err2.d: The rook trades rooks on d8, and the attack is over: the game is level. The h-file is open for the other rook; look at h7.
The rook leaves d6 without check, and Black gains time to bring defenders: the game is level. The h-file is open for the other rook; look at h7.
